terms.comment: Short for mīles veterānus, an old, tried soldier; legiōnēs veterānae are legions of them (Caes. B.G. 1.24). As an adjective, old and seasoned in general: bovēs (Varro), vītis (Columella). Traupman gives a feminine veterāna.

terms.gloss: soldier who has served out his time
terms.comment: From ēmerēre, to serve out one’s time; ēmerita stīpendia are completed years of service (Sall. Jug. 84.2). The stress is on finished service, as with a pensioner.

phrases.latin: Avus meus veterānus est; multōs annōs mīlitāvit.
phrases.english: My grandfather is a veteran: he served many years in the army.
